title: The gym fights back
body: Gym battles were a click-Attack-twenty-times chore. Now every round the leader's Pokémon shows its next move — a hit, a big hit, a brace or a charge — and you answer with one of five: Strike, Power, Guard, Focus or Type Burst. Guard a hit and you counter; Focus through a brace; Power through a charge to break it. Three perfect reads and your next blow crits.

Eight rounds, then the bell — more HP left wins on decision. Types matter both ways (bring Water to Brock, not Fire), and each leader has a trick: Koga poisons, Blaine burns, Erika drains, Lt. Surge charges, Sabrina hides her hand. Every round is a picture.

title: The reels spin again
body: Slots lost their motion in the rebuild — one still frame, then the result. Now the machine itself animates: the reels scroll past with motion blur, slow down and land one at a time, left to right, with a glowing "two down, one to go" tease when the first two match, and the win line lights up on the result. About three seconds a spin, like the old machine.
Under the hood, 8,600 lines of retired code left the bot. Nothing you use changed.

title: Reminders that keep reminding, and a tidy-up
body: /reminder used to DM you exactly once per cooldown, ever. It now fires every time a cooldown ends, and covers the daily, pack energy, quiz, mystery box, journey, card drops and votes.

/setchannel needs Manage Server now (any member could move a server's drop channel before) and checks the bot can actually post there. /itemshop has Buy buttons. /report is rate-limited and kept safe. /vote checks your cooldown before calling out, and its reward posts publicly.

Retired: /resetpack (charged 40 coins for nothing since Pack Energy), /avatarchoice, /announcesets, /claimgift and /tint. Cards that /tint had pointed at expiring Discord links are back on their real art.

title: No house fee
body: Market sales and auctions pay the seller the full price. The few fees taken today have been refunded.

title: Mystery box, card drops, the journey and your bag
body: /mysterybox hands out a Fusion Token you can actually spend (the old box stored it under the wrong name — those stranded tokens are now usable), gives cards with a condition and a date, only from released sets, and scores season points.
/pickcard drops three cards as a picture; one each, the dropper gets a two-second head start, and a claim can't be lost to a restart.

/journey rewards are what the story says — a rare card is rare, tokens go to your bag, trinkets are kept — and a run you abandon expires after a day instead of skipping the cooldown forever. /bag shows packs, tokens, energy, badges and trinkets.
/duelprofile is a proper record with the top duelists. /deck is retired: duels never used it.

title: Leaderboards, quests, achievements and the season, rebuilt
body: /leaderboard is a picture with medals and avatars, per server or across all servers, with your own rank underneath — cards, coins, gem mints, XP, streaks, season points and aura. Half-point grades count now, and coins-only players are ranked too. /serverleaderboard races the servers by the players who actually use the bot there.
/quests: eight quests in the pool (forging, gym wins, pack buys and quiz answers included), the same three for everyone each day, and a claim button that keeps working after a restart.
/achievements is paged with progress bars, and an achievement you just earned is announced instead of silently ticked.
/season pays the top three when the month ends — automatically. The August podium, which had gone unpaid, is paid now.

title: Trades and auctions, rebuilt
body: /trade is a table you can see: both offers as cards, coins on either side, lock and accept. Offered cards are held so nothing else can move them, the trade survives a restart, and the final swap re-checks everything before anything changes hands.

/auction keeps the card in your binder while it runs, holds bids until you're outbid (refunded automatically), extends the clock when a bid lands in the last two minutes, lets the seller cancel while there are no bids, and settles by itself. Bid from the auction post or the numbered board. The one auction that was open has been moved over.

title: The market works again — and five lost cards are back
body: Listing a card used to move it out of your binder, and every purchase then failed because "the seller no longer owns it" — deleting the listing and the card. Nobody ever completed a market sale. A listing is now a price tag on a card that stays in your binder until it sells; the five cards that vanished this way have been put back with their owners.

/market browse is a numbered board with buy buttons, purchases post publicly, sellers get a DM, big sales reach the drop channel, and /market trend (or /cardtrend) charts real sales. The house keeps 5% of each sale.

/sell re-checks every card when you confirm and pays only for what actually left; SIR and non-holo filters work. /give has confirmations, a 1,000-coin gift cap, 2,000 a day and a minute between gifts — gifted coins no longer count as earned. /fuse works again (it was looking for the wrong token) with a preview of the odds. /swapcodes refuses locked, listed, graded or traded cards.

title: Slots, quiz and Who's That Pokémon, rebuilt
body: Slots: Pokémon symbols on real reels with a printed paytable — Caterpie ×3 up to Dragonite ×50, any pair ×1.5 — a bet cap of 500, and Spin-again buttons. The old machine had no cap and paid out more than it took.
Quiz: ten distinct questions, your own scoreboard (two players at once no longer scramble each other's score), coins and aura per right answer, pack energy every three in a row.

Who's That Pokémon is now a room game: the silhouette is public, anyone can press Guess, the first right answer takes the round, hints appear on the card, coins for every solve (capped per day) and a scoreboard at the end.
Duel pictures no longer show boxes where the icons should be.

title: Blackjack, rebuilt
body: A new table: no more boxes where the icons should be, the corner indices sit inside the cards, and a Pokémon deals — Meowth most nights.
Double down on your first two cards, play again straight from the result, and a private record of your hands. A hand nobody finishes now stands on its own instead of handing the bet back.

title: Labels take colour too
body: A colour from your palette can go on the label of a slab as well as the case — Galaxy case, Gold label. Same roll, same palette, your choice where.
The label's text picks its own ink from whatever is painted under it, so a Poké Ball label stays readable.

title: Case colours for your slabs
body: Every graded card sits in a clear case — now /slab roll gives it a colour. Six tiers, 58 colours, five shades for the solids: Frost and Slate are everywhere, Obsidian Black is one in four hundred, Void and Master Ball one in a few thousand.
Colours land in a palette; paint one onto any slab, strip it back off, melt the ones you don't want. A Gem Mint 10 comes back from the graders with a free roll.

title: The forge replaces crafting
body: Crafting was a vending machine. Now every recipe wants dust AND spare ingredients from the same set, and the forge is a roll: a Holo comes out 60% of the time, a Special Illustration 45%.
Boosts buy better odds for more dust. A misfire eats the ingredients, refunds a quarter of the dust and spits out a random card one rarity down. A Pristine result is a Perfect Forge.

title: Server drops can be claimed again
body: Pressing Claim on a dropped pack said "too late" within seconds — the claim was looking up the wrong key. Every drop since launch was unclaimable. Fixed.

title: Peek spares are capped at 3 a day
body: Taking a spare out of someone else's pack is limited to 3 per player per day — free cards were unlimited before.
Nothing changes for the opener: you still earn coins and energy every time a friend peeks.

title: Sunday round-up
body: Every Sunday your server gets one picture: the week's top three collectors, the rarest pull, the best grade back and the set everyone is chasing.
Nothing to set up — it posts itself.

title: New sets arrive with a poster
body: Every weekly set now lands with its three chase cards, the card count and how many holos are inside.
One button on the post makes it your chase set.

title: Gym fights work again
body: /gym and every battle button were dead. Fixed — along with SIR cards missing Power Strike and a double payout on a fast double click.
Also fixed: /swapcodes, /cardtrend, inventory filters, and blackjack and /pickcard timing out.

title: Wishlist hunt board
body: Pin up to eight cards to a MOST WANTED board your server can see, with the real odds on each one.
Pull one and it's a WISH GRANTED: +25 coins, +10 XP. Pull someone else's and they hear about your spare.

title: Out in the open
body: Grading orders, wishlist pins, level-ups and achievements now post where the room can see them.
Errors, pickers and your ledger stay private.

title: Pack Energy replaces the timer
body: The 20-minute wait is gone: hold up to 3 packs, with one coming back every 2 hours.
Earn more from /daily, gym wins, Peeks, votes and quiz streaks — stacking up to 6.

title: The grading house
body: Four sub-grades — centering, corners, edges, surface — and the lowest one sets your grade. Four 10s is a Black Label.
Four lanes from Economy to Super Express, pricing that moves with the queue, real cert numbers and a printed slab.

title: New pack reveal, Peek and binders
body: Packs open as a five-card spread with the best pull lifted out of the row.
A spare goes to the first server-mate who claims it, /showcase prints your top nine, and Holo Weekend doubles bonus holo odds.

title: 127 sets, 17,000 cards
body: The full expansion catalog is staged in print order.
A new set goes live every week — /upcoming shows what's next.
